blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C2):** eu consigo ler, ouvir, falar e escrever sobre linguagem simples na administração pública a partir de um editorial, defendendo reformas com argumentos e exemplos.

body: Esta aula treina **escrever frases claras e corretas (IELTS Writing, TOEFL Writing)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: Editorial: Say It Plainly, Minister
paras: Every year, millions of citizens **lose benefits** they are owed, **not because they are ineligible but because they cannot decode the form**. Consider a recent notice: “**Pursuant to the aforementioned provisions, claimants are hereby required to furnish documentation…**” **What it means**: send us your papers.

Government has **a duty to be understood**. **Were** every agency to **adopt plain-language standards**, **fewer claims would be rejected** and **fewer calls would clog** helplines. **Critics argue** that simplification **dilutes** precision; **in fact**, vague writing is **the real threat to precision**. A law that no one can read is **barely a law at all**.

blocks.body: Editoriais fortes **antecipam a objeção** (*Critics argue*) e a **refutam** (*in fact*). O exemplo concreto vale mais que a generalização.
*Aforementioned* e *hereby* são marcas de jargão: o editorial os cita para criticar.

items.s: Citizens lose benefits not because they are ineligible ___ because they cannot decode the form. (but)
___ every agency to adopt plain language, fewer claims would fail. (were)
Vague writing is the real ___ to precision. (threat)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

items.ans: In plain English send your papers
items.pt: Em inglês simples: mande seus papéis.

body: **Cut through the red tape.** — Cortar a burocracia.
**Say it plainly.** — Dizer de forma simples.
**Spell it out.** — Explicar com todas as letras.
**Plain as day.** — Claro como o dia.
**Fall through the net.** — Escapar do sistema.
**Black and white.** — Preto no branco.
**Lost in the small print.** — Perdido nas letras miúdas.
**Read the room.** — Perceber o contexto.
**Make sense of.** — Dar sentido a.
**Call a spade a spade.** — Chamar as coisas pelo nome.
**Pursuant to what, exactly?** — Nos termos de quê, exatamente?
**In plain English: send your papers.** — Em inglês simples: mande seus papéis.
**I got a notice I could not understand.** — Recebi um aviso que não entendi.

items.label: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances
items.note: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances: o acento muda o sentido (He said she STOLE it × he said SHE stole it) e as pausas separam ideias técnicas densas.
words: I didn’t SAY he did it.
I didn’t say HE did it.
I didn’t say he DID it.

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence editorial paragraph urging an institution to use plain language, with a concrete example and a rebutted objection.
blocks.model: Our bank’s letters are unreadable. Consider the phrase “subject to the foregoing, the account shall be deemed dormant.” It means: we will freeze your account. Critics argue that plain wording is less accurate; in fact, vague wording causes mistakes. Were the bank to rewrite its letters, fewer customers would lose money. Clarity is a service, not a luxury.
